newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says Archer tax plan does not pass test.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says Archer tax plan does not pass test.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday said a new Republican tax cut plan did not meet his criteria and violated the balanced budget pact he hammered out in May with the Republican-led Congress.

"I have reviewed this plan and I believe that in its present form it does not meet the tests that I would hold myself to," Clinton said of the tax programme unveiled Monday by Bill Archer, the influential Republican who chairs the House Ways and Means Committee that writes tax legislation.

Speaking at an unrelated White House event, Clinton listed his tests as the following: "One, being faithful to the budget agreement; second, having a tax cut that will grow the economy; third, having a tax cut that is fair to middle class families; and, fourth, having a tax cut that genuinely helps to increase the quality and volume of education in America."

Top U.S. officials blasted the $85 billion tax cut plan on Monday, but Clinton's remarks were his first on the plan, which fleshes out the outlines of the budget agreement Clinton and the Republicans hammered out in May.

Clinton said Archer's plan violated that pact by reducing the overall tax cuts for higher education. "It falls $13 billion short in the amount of higher education tax cuts specifically agreed to in the balanced budget agreement," he said. "We agreed to roughly $35 billion. You might say that $34 billion is roughly $35 billion, but $22 billion is not."
The president also criticized the Archer plan's treatment of his "Hope Scholarships" proposal and of a proposed $500 per child tax credit.
